 KSR Staff Predictions: No. 23 Kentucky vs. Central Florida
 KSR 6h 0 Share Share 
 Kentucky’s third and final exhibition of the preseason is another Big 12 matchup. Can the Wildcats make it a clean 3-0?
 Central Florida comes to Rupp Arena tonight to battle Mark Pope ‘s squad. Kentucky, ranked No. 23 in the country, took care of Little Rock in the first exhibition before putting together a better performance in a win over No. 19 Texas Tech. What kind of challenge will UCF present? Former Duke Blue Devil Johnny Dawkins is Knights’ head coach. Dior Johnson , a major blast from the recruiting past, is on the roster after transferring from Tarleton State. He’s not the only name the Big Blue Nation will be familiar with, either.
 This is the Wildcats’ final tune-up before the real thing begins next Tuesday against Manhattan. KSR gives their thoughts on how it will go down with our Parlour Pizza Pregame Predictions.
 Zack Geoghegan
 What a fascinating roster Johnny Dawkins has put together as he enters year 11 as UCF’s head coach. Only five players return from last season’s team that made the NCAA Tournament. That group included former Wildcat Jordan Burks, who is now at Oklahoma State. Dawkins retooled in the portal, headlined by the return of Dior Johnson and his scoring punch. This is a group projected to finish 13th in the Big 12 standings.
 Kentucky looked much improved from the first exhibition to the second. My only hope is to see that continue tonight. I feel good about where Milan Momcilovic and Mason Williams are at. Alex Wilkins, Malachi Moreno, and Ousmane N’Diaye have shown plenty of positive flashes. Let’s see if Zoom Diallo can settle in and have a mini-breakout performance. Reaching 30 three-point attempts would be nice to see, too.
 Much like the first two exhibitions, I’m not expecting Mark Pope to open the playbook much. These games are about working on areas that need it. It won’t exactly be pretty, but we’ll be leaving Rupp Arena with another win for the ‘Cats. 
 Score: Kentucky 75, UCF 69 
 Nick Roush
 Even though UCF made last year’s NCAA Tournament, this iteration of the Golden Knights isn’t passing muster. They lost to a 6-man LSU team and barely escaped with a win over a D-II team. 
 This game is all about Kentucky. The most important goal is getting Zoom Diallo going. I think it happens tonight for the Kentucky point guard, who will finish with 13 points and 6 assists in a victory that is never in doubt. 
 Score: Kentucky 78, UCF 66 
 Adam Luckett 
 UCF surprised many by earning an at-large bid out of the Big 12 last season, but head coach Johnny Dawkins was forced to go shopping in the portal to reload. This is not the most resourced program in college basketball. The Knights are trying to win in the margins. What you can expect is a team that will play with pace.
 This is a good challenge early for Kentucky after a solid win against Texas Tech. John Bol (7-foot-2, No. 1 in Big 12 in defensive rebound percentage) will give Malachi Moreno a legit challenge in the paint, but the Cats will have a major size advantage at every other position. The Knights will likely struggle in the half-court, but UK’s endurance and discipline will be tested by tempo.
 UK gets out to an early lead but the road team hangs around throughout 40 minutes. Both teams squeeze off over 30 three-point attempts in this game. If any squad gets hot, that could change the game, but the Wildcats ultimately make their size difference count. 
 The Cats respond with a strong rebounding game. Zoom Diallo bounces back strongly against a smaller lineup. Kentucky wins by double-digits.
 Score: Kentucky 82, UCF 70 
 Drew Franklin
 It’s time for Kentucky to put up more points in the preseason. After scoring 69 against Little Rock and then 76 against No. 19 Texas Tech, the Wildcats will go even higher against UCF, which allowed 74 to Rollins just a few days ago. This will be a Milan Momcilovic game. UK’s sharpshooter took the fifth-most shots in the Texas Tech win. Let’s pump those numbers up tonight and get him the most looks. He’ll score 20+ if they do.
 With Momcilovic getting buckets, Kentucky will roll past UCF to wrap up the three-game exhibition slate. We’ll also see a better Zoom Diallo game to hush his critics, plus a more efficient evening from Alex Wilkins .
 A fun night is ahead, then the action gets real next week.
 Kentucky 86, UCF 70 
 Jeff Drummond
 The Cats took a nice step forward between the first two exhibition games, and one would hope to see that again tonight.
 Two things to watch for me: a better job on the glass (especially limiting UCF’s offensive rebounds and second-chance opportunities) and getting Zoom Diallo some confidence going into the regular season.
 I think we might see a breakout offensive performance from UK with a ton of 3s. 
 Kentucky 101, UCF 78 
 Justin Rowland
 Through two exhibitions for both teams I don’t know that I’m quite as confident as some others about how this one will play out. UCF hasn’t been too impressive to date, I’ll grant that. Rollins is not impressive and LSU was limited to say the least.
 We haven’t seen things really click completely for Kentucky through the exhibition season. The backcourt parts haven’t looked great together at the same time. I’ll call for that to look as good as it has to this point in the year. It’s probably not reasonable to expect both Zoom Diallo and Alex Wilkins to play well together on the same night yet, because both are trying to get on track and acclimated to the offense. 
 I do think it’s likely that UK gets Milan Momcilovic on track tonight. 
 Kentucky 83, UCF 70 
 Steven Peake
 We’ve made it to the final exhibition before things get serious next week. These aren’t Tacko Fall’s UCF Knights. This Central Florida team lost to an LSU squad that used just six players and then squeaked past Rollins. Kentucky should handle this team.
 Tonight, I want to see the Cats get out to a hot start. Let’s see how good this offense looks when shots are falling in the first half. Give me crisp ball movement, open looks, and a few threes that actually go in before halftime.
 An exhibition win won’t tell us everything, but I’d like to head into next week feeling good about what Kentucky is building. I think the Cats take control early and give us a comfortable win to close out the preseason.
 Score: Kentucky 89, UCF 67 
 Jack Pilgrim
 Central Florida is picked to finish 14th in the Big 12 and lost to a six-player LSU roster in its first exhibition game before struggling to put away Division II Rollins College in the second, winning by six. The Knights have some fine pieces, led by blast from the past Dior Johnson—now at his 12th program since the start of high school—but they shouldn’t be able to contain Kentucky’s firepower. This needs to be a feel-good evening for the Wildcats at Rupp Arena, with their better-than-anticipated defensive efficiency staying right where it is, but their offense finally coming together for an explosion.
 Zoom Diallo has taken some heat for his play through two exhibition games, and I expect the conversation to shift some after tonight. Mason Williams is ahead of schedule, but UK invested heavily in Diallo as a portal addition, and we’re going to see why for the first time tonight—with more of the same out of Alex Wilkins, who has popped in early viewings. We’re gonna see PG1’s best tonight, while also hitting 15 3-pointers in a blowout victory to close out exhibition play and move on to the regular season.
 Kentucky 96, UCF 69
